criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: new tests pass. They show that an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and that an unknown category is still rejected with the list including `mistake`.
criteria.evidence: I ran these tests and they passed. records::tests::mistake_is_a_category_and_unknown_ones_stay_unknown checks that parse("mistake") works, that ALL has 9 entries and contains Mistake, and that parse("bogus") returns None. lifecycle::the_mistake_category_is_accepted_and_an_unknown_one_is_refused_with_the_list checks that intervene with category mistake succeeds, and that intervene with category bogus fails with an error naming both 'bogus' and 'mistake'.
commands: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test introspection --test lifecycle mistake

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows that status and the audit output report mistake counts per class and per cause, and that the JSON has those breakdowns separate from `interventions_by_category`.
criteria.evidence: The status half is shown. mistakes_are_counted_per_class_and_cause_and_repeat_causes_share_one_proposal checks status --json (mistakes.total 3, by_class, by_cause[0].count 2, with interventions_by_category kept separate as mistake 2 and other 1) and the status text. The audit half is not shown: no test runs `athena audit` with mistakes. A search for 'mistake' in crates/athena-cli/tests/auditor.rs finds nothing, and a search for '"audit"' across the CLI tests finds nothing. The planned demonstration promised to check the audit output and did not.
commands: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test introspection --test lifecycle mistake

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention produces a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. Repeat causes aggregate into one proposal.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. It checks that every prompt carries category mistake and the instruction 'check or knowledge that would have prevented it', and that the stored introspection has a non-empty prevention. It also checks that two mistakes sharing a failure class come out as one by_cause entry (count 2, recurring) with a single prevention_kind and prevention.
commands: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test introspection --test lifecycle mistake

criteria.criterion: Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' (the eleven back-filled on 2026-10-23) are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
criteria.evidence: Intervention::is_mistake in records.rs carries a doc comment stating the prefix rule. mistake_report is the one counting function, used by both status and Athena::mistakes, and audit calls Athena::mistakes. The introspection test seeds an 'other' record whose text starts 'Mistake:' and checks that it is counted and that its file is byte-identical afterwards. Two caveats: audit prints mistakes only when athena.audit(job) returns Some, and the audit path is not tested. The eleven real records cannot be checked here because records/ is absent from the snapshot.

Tests check that these lines appear in the status text. Status output meets the criterion.

findings.summary: Criterion 2 requires a test showing that the audit output reports mistakes per class and per cause; no such test exists.
findings.evidence: The new tests check only `athena status` and the status JSON. crates/athena-cli/tests/auditor.rs has no mention of mistake, and no CLI test checks audit output for mistakes. The planned demonstration said it would read the audit output with a stub model, and it does not.

findings.summary: The audit prints the mistake report only when a job audit is produced.
findings.evidence: In main.rs Command::Audit, the code returns early with `let Some(audited) = athena.audit(&job)? else { return Ok(0); };` before printing mistakes. When there is no audit, the mistake counts never appear. This untested path is where they would go missing.

summary: The change adds the `mistake` category and counts records of category `other` whose text starts 'Mistake:' through Intervention::is_mistake, without rewriting any record. Status and its JSON now show a mistakes report per class and per cause, with recurring causes marked and the proposed prevention printed. Introspecting a mistake now asks the model for the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. I ran the new tests, fmt and clippy; all pass. Criterion 2 is not met: it requires a test showing that the audit output reports the per-class and per-cause counts, and no test runs audit with mistakes, although the planned demonstration promised one. The audit also skips the mistake report when no job audit is produced. A minor scope finding: docs/design/athena-v0.md changed but is not on the deliverables list. The verdict is fail until an audit-output test is added.
